objects.start
objects are the main element that
make up your game, they're the
things that store and execute your
code, display your models, and more! They
function similarly to scratch sprites if that
helps.
objects can be created from the scene tool-
bar, they have certain parameters like
name, spawn point, and their 3d-type: which
there are two types of, 3d, and static3d.
3d is the default, and static3d can be useful
and even neccessary for some model types.
you can also interact with them via the
inspector (on the left,) click on them in the
scene, or using the properties tab on the side-
bar (on the right)
the way objects work is by storing a bunch of
data, these variables can range from assigned
files to transformation, some variables can
even be added by scripts, that's how local
variables work! Cameras are also objects,
just with some extra metadata

cameras are the connection

you can use a camera by assigning it, either

local var.start
local variables are variables that
are stored in an object that runs
a script, yes, they can be read via
code from other objects, but without that
they're simply stored in that object's data-
repo, which also contains neat stuff like
some internal variables from the
object; x, y, z, rx...
local variables can be read and written to.
you can read one by using it as an input, and
you can write to them using a `set variable`
block, just remember that you need to set a
variable before reading it if it doesn't exist
yet, so basically instancing it. That doesn't
apply to data_return though
(a built-in local variable used for returning
and storing data)
as now in g3dce it's created when trying to
read it, it'll even give you a neat little
message :)
if you'd rather use global variables for
readable data between all scripts, you can
create a global variable in the toolbar in
the script editor, and read them using inputs.
or you can manipulate them more in the global
variables category
